key_insight: AIPatient Arena shows that medical LLMs can sound strong in interviews and explanations, but still struggle with diagnostic reasoning, uncertainty, and complete information gathering across real consultation workflows.
clinical_relevance: For clinical AI, this suggests evaluation should measure the full consultation process—not just final answers—before considering deployment in patient-facing settings.
method: Built an EHR-grounded evaluation framework using patient-specific knowledge graphs.
Simulated multi-turn physician-patient consultations across eight competence dimensions.
Tested on a primary cohort of 437 patients plus two out-of-distribution validation cohorts (119 and 67).
evidence_signal: LLMs scored highest on questioning, ethics, and explanation quality, but weaker on ambiguous responses, information coverage, and diagnostic accuracy, even when richer context was provided.
watch_item: Workflow performance may still fail in real settings if models repeat questions, miss past history, or handle uncertainty poorly, so deployment needs careful oversight and validation.
paper_title: AIPatient Arena: EHR-grounded evaluation of large language models in end-to-end clinical consultation workflows
